crop.notes: Whole 'The Prize Ring' item; an unrelated one-line baseball telegraph item sits above it.

ocr.notes: Gist readable; several garbled phrases in Goss's letter (e.g. 'fight nea eyaare stand-up fight' for 'fight me a square stand-up fight', 'money stake').

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Globe-Democrat printed Joe Goss's New York challenge to Tom Allen for the championship of the world at $1,000 a side, London prize ring rules, and reported Allen had wired Goss to meet him in Cincinnati May 12 to sign articles.

metadata.notes: Masthead: St. Louis Daily Globe-Democrat, Thursday Morning, May 4, 1876, page 8.

facts.fact: Joe Goss, 'Champion of England', challenged Allen from New York to a fight under London prize ring rules for the championship of the world and $1,000 a side, the fight to be four months after signing articles
Goss said he could not fight sooner than four months because he was engaged to travel with Jem Mace in Howes & Cushing's circus
Goss was reported to have deposited $500 with Eph Holland in Cincinnati to make a match with Allen
Allen telegraphed Goss that he would meet him in Cincinnati on May 12 to draw up articles for a fight

notes: The paper doubts Goss's Cincinnati deposit is real. Allen's telegram is reported secondhand from a Cincinnati telegram.
